articles.title: First Person: Syrians lead efforts to clear rubble and rebuild lives
articles.summary: Communities in Syria are clearing rubble and rebuilding neighbourhoods and livelihoods torn down in the more than a decade of conflict and crisis in the country.
articles.content:
The conflict there killed hundreds of thousands of people, displaced millions, and caused severe damage to infrastructure across the country estimated at over $100 billion.

Joelle-Seme Park works for the UN Development Programme (UNDP) and recently travelled to Syria to visit recovery projects.

“Standing in the middle of a neighbourhood in Rural Damascus, it was hard to imagine what daily life here once looked like.

Piles of broken concrete and twisted metal block almost everything. Roads remain closed. Water and sewage networks cannot be repaired. Power and essential services struggle to return. Entire communities stay disconnected.

© UNDP Syria

Streets are blocked by rubble. Buildings have collapsed. Shops are shuttered.

Tweet URL

Even moving from one street to another is difficult.

One thing became clear to me; until rubble is removed, life cannot fully restart.

Communities are driving efforts to clear rubble, yet they cannot do it alone.

Clearing debris requires equipment, planning, coordination and sustained support.

Through the REVIVE project, UNDP and its partners are helping communities take those first steps forward.

The project is clearing 570,000 tonnes of debris across Aleppo, Deir-ez-Zor, Homs and Rural Damascus, while rehabilitating roads, water and sewage networks, providing explosive ordnance risk education and supporting debris recycling initiatives that turn rubble into construction materials.

Rebuilding communities and lives

Across the communities I visited, the pattern was consistent; once rubble is removed, life begins to return.

Movement resumes. Access is restored. Families begin coming home.

This work also provides something many families urgently need: a source of income.

So far, more than 1,300 people have participated in cash-for-work activities linked to debris removal, helping support over 6,000 family members.

One woman I spoke to who was working at a debris recycling facility in Aleppo told me how that before the project she had no income to support her family, but that now she can provide food and medicine for her children, niece and nephew. She also said they are now back in school.

© UNDP/Giles Clarke

Beyond the income, there is also pride in helping restore a neighbourhood. In reopening a street. In seeing visible progress where so much has been disrupted.

A community volunteer I met in Aleppo said that after the debris removal, local people volunteered to rebuild a park and streetlights, allowing children and women to enjoy this space after school, without fear and in peace.

What stood out most to me was not only the scale of the work, but the determination of communities themselves, with people removing debris from their homes with their bare hands.

In Syria, clearing debris is not only about removing what was destroyed. It is about reopening roads, reconnecting services, supporting livelihoods and helping communities regain a sense of normal life again.”

articles.personality_title: Syrian communities lead the way in clearing rubble and rebuilding homes
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Syria has faced more than ten years of conflict that caused huge damage. Many people lost their homes, and roads, water, and electricity systems were broken. The damage is very expensive to fix, costing over $100 billion.

**What happened** – The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) started a project called REVIVE to help Syrian communities clear away the rubble left by the fighting. They have removed 570,000 tonnes of debris in cities like Aleppo and Damascus. The project also fixes roads and water systems and teaches people how to stay safe from leftover explosives. More than 1,300 people have worked in this cleanup, earning money to support their families.

**Impact** – Clearing the rubble makes it easier for families to return home and for communities to reconnect. It helps reopen streets and restore services like water and electricity. The work also gives people jobs and hope. For example, a woman in Aleppo who now works recycling rubble can buy food and medicine for her children and send them back to school. Volunteers have even rebuilt parks and streetlights, making neighborhoods safer and more welcoming.

**What's next step** – The project will continue to clear debris and repair infrastructure in more areas. As roads and services come back, more families can return to their homes. The community efforts may inspire further rebuilding and recovery across Syria.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Syrian communities, supported by the UNDP, are removing rubble and repairing infrastructure to rebuild their neighborhoods and lives after years of conflict.
articles.personality_title_fr: Les communautés syriennes montrent la voie en déblayant les décombres et reconstruisant les maisons
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – La Syrie a subi plus de dix ans de conflit qui ont causé d’énormes dégâts. Beaucoup de personnes ont perdu leur maison, et les routes, les réseaux d’eau et d’électricité ont été endommagés. Les réparations coûtent plus de 100 milliards de dollars.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) a lancé un projet appelé REVIVE pour aider les communautés syriennes à déblayer les décombres laissés par les combats. Ils ont retiré 570 000 tonnes de débris dans des villes comme Alep et Damas. Le projet répare aussi les routes et les réseaux d’eau, et forme les habitants à la sécurité face aux explosifs restants. Plus de 1 300 personnes ont travaillé à ce nettoyage, gagnant de l’argent pour soutenir leurs familles.

**Impact** – Enlever les décombres facilite le retour des familles chez elles et la reconnexion des communautés. Cela permet de rouvrir les rues et de rétablir les services comme l’eau et l’électricité. Ce travail offre aussi des emplois et de l’espoir. Par exemple, une femme à Alep qui travaille maintenant au recyclage des débris peut acheter de la nourriture et des médicaments pour ses enfants et les envoyer à l’école. Des bénévoles ont même reconstruit des parcs et des lampadaires, rendant les quartiers plus sûrs et accueillants.

**Prochaine étape** – Le projet va continuer à enlever les débris et réparer les infrastructures dans d’autres régions. Au fur et à mesure que les routes et services reviennent, plus de familles pourront retourner chez elles. Ces efforts communautaires pourraient inspirer d’autres reconstructions à travers la Syrie.

**En une phrase** – Les communautés syriennes, soutenues par le PNUD, enlèvent les décombres et réparent les infrastructures pour reconstruire leurs quartiers et leurs vies après des années de conflit.
articles.personality_title_es: Las comunidades sirias lideran la limpieza de escombros y la reconstrucción de hogares
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Siria ha sufrido más de diez años de conflicto que causaron grandes daños. Muchas personas perdieron sus hogares, y las carreteras, el agua y los sistemas eléctricos quedaron dañados. Reparar todo cuesta más de 100 mil millones de dólares.

**Qué pasó** – El Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) inició un proyecto llamado REVIVE para ayudar a las comunidades sirias a limpiar los escombros dejados por la guerra. Han retirado 570,000 toneladas de escombros en ciudades como Alepo y Damasco. El proyecto también repara caminos y sistemas de agua, y enseña a las personas a estar seguras ante explosivos que quedaron. Más de 1,300 personas han trabajado en esta limpieza, ganando dinero para apoyar a sus familias.

**Impacto** – Quitar los escombros facilita que las familias regresen a sus hogares y que las comunidades se reconecten. Ayuda a reabrir calles y a restaurar servicios como el agua y la electricidad. El trabajo también ofrece empleos y esperanza. Por ejemplo, una mujer en Alepo que ahora trabaja reciclando escombros puede comprar comida y medicinas para sus hijos y enviarlos de nuevo a la escuela. Los voluntarios incluso han reconstruido parques y faroles, haciendo los vecindarios más seguros y agradables.

**Próximo paso** – El proyecto continuará limpiando escombros y reparando infraestructuras en más áreas. A medida que las calles y los servicios vuelvan, más familias podrán regresar a sus hogares. Estos esfuerzos comunitarios pueden inspirar más reconstrucción y recuperación en Siria.

**Resumen en una frase** – Las comunidades sirias, con apoyo del PNUD, están quitando escombros y reparando infraestructuras para reconstruir sus barrios y vidas después de años de conflicto.
